summary: The change makes the MessagePack analyzer keep validating [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types while skipping source generation for them. The three F1 contract-diagnostic tests pass and the F2 test (source-generation-only diagnostics not reported) passes, but the analyzer still crashes with AD0001 on duplicate string keys in a suppressed type, so the full suite fails one new test and N1 is not met; tests.fail_without_fix was not run, so N2 cannot be determined.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: All three F1 tests pass on head: MemberWithoutKeyIsReported (MsgPack004), MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported (MsgPack003), and AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported (MsgPack015); the duplicate-key diagnostic MsgPack005 is also reported (the duplicate-string test fails only on the extra analyzer-crash diagnostic, tracked under N1).

SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed passes on head, and the code skips the AOT init-property check when suppressed (line 989) and returns before the partial-type check when SuppressSourceGeneration is true (lines 1383-1386).

The full suite fails because DuplicateStringKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure produces a second diagnostic AD0001 (analyzer crash) in addition to the expected MsgPack005, so the analyzer still crashes on duplicate string keys in a suppressed type.

The tests.fail_without_fix check was not run for this revision, so it cannot be established that the new tests fail without the fix and pass with it; additionally DuplicateStringKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure fails on head, so pass-with-fix does not hold for every new test.

findings.title: Analyzer crashes (AD0001) on duplicate string keys in a suppressed type
findings.claim: GetObjectInfo reports MsgPack005 for the duplicate key but then executes `if (true) { stringMembers.Add(...) }` for properties, which throws ArgumentException on the already-existing key and crashes the analyzer, producing an extra AD0001 diagnostic. The intMembers and field-stringMembers branches guard with ContainsKey, but the property stringMembers branch does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Change line 1039 from `if (true)` to `if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey))` so the property branch matches the intMembers and field branches and does not re-add an already-reported duplicate key.

findings.title: Inconsistent duplicate-key guard and dead `if (true)` block
findings.claim: The property branch wraps stringMembers.Add in `if (true)` (always true), while the equivalent intMembers and field-stringMembers branches use `if (!ContainsKey(...))`. The `if (true)` block is dead-looking code and is the direct cause of finding N1.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `if (true)` with `if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey))` for consistency with the other two branches.
